newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close sharply higher, banks star.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close sharply higher, banks star.

text.p: French stocks finished sharply up, with a shove from bank stocks after strong first-half results, healthy oil share performance and a tug from rising bonds in the wake of weaker-than-expected U.S. economic inflation data.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended 27.31 points or 1.34 percent up at 2,065.37 while the CAC-40 futures contract closed 20 points up from Wednesday at 2066.0.
Volume was a healthy 5.42 billion francs.
U.S. producer price data for August was benign in terms of the prospects for U.S. interest rate increase and franc firmness bolstered the bourse, traders said.
Oil and bank stocks buoyed activity, while cyclical stocks also gained on the back of expectations of economic improvement, they said.
Profit-taking could set in on Friday before release of U.S. consumer price figures, they added.
*BNP closes 3.0 francs or 1.58 percent higher at 192.5 with a hefty 1.76 million shares traded. First-half net attributable profit largely surpassed expectations.
BNP's reported an 80 percent rise in net attributable profit to 1.735 billion. CCF also reported a profit rise.
Analysts judge first rise in net banking income in two years at BNP seen as sign of better outlook for bank results in 1996. Societe Generale up 1.56 percent at 585 francs.
*UAP, a key BNP shareholder, firmed on back of BNP figures.
*Eurotunnel jumped in afternoon on market talk of a debt deal coming closer and further reporting on debt talks in British Evening Standard newspaper.
*Total firmed with oil price rise on Iraq trouble.
